definition: Candor means openness and honesty in speech.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word candor. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know candor should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The chef answered the health inspector with unexpected candor, pointing out two violations the inspection itself had missed.
Tact is the gentlest rung, far milder than candor — tact trims and times the truth to spare feelings, telling only as much as the moment can bear.
Honesty stops short of candor: honesty answers truthfully when asked, while candor volunteers the uncomfortable truth before anyone asks.

Frankness is plain, unguarded speech — saying what you actually think, with a hint of bluntness about it. Candor shares that plainness but adds the volunteering: candor offers the uncomfortable truth before anyone asks for it, while frankness only promises directness once a person has decided to speak.

Openness is a general willingness to share — information, feelings, plans — in speech or in manner. Candor is narrower and costlier: candor volunteers the damaging detail in plain words, unasked. An open person shares readily on most things; candor means honesty precisely where sharing hurts.

Most expedition guides sell the summit.
Elena Marquez, who has led forty parties up the mountain, sells the turnaround.
At the first briefing she hands each climber a card listing the three points where she has turned parties back, and the storm, the year before, that taught her to do it.
Clients are often startled by her candor: she will tell a paying customer, on day one, that his pack weight and his pace make him the likeliest person on the roster to be sent down.
'People pay me for the mountain,' she says, 'but they survive me because nobody hears a comfortable version of anything.' Her bookings have a waiting list.
